summary: Dairy plant wants to investigate whether optical spectroscopy can track protein concentration in a whey stream ahead of a concentration stage, using laboratory results as reference, with a first measurement concept that copes with the stream turning turbid rather than assuming it stays clear.

facts_stated.text: The stream is whey, nominally relatively clear.
The measurement point sits before a concentration stage.
The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions

targets.variable: change of protein concentration over time

optical_regime.enquiry_quote: The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions

customer_premises.claim: Spectroscopy can track protein concentration in this stream as it changes.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: whether spectroscopy can track protein concentration as the stream changes

customer_premises.claim: One measurement concept will cope with the stream changing from clear to turbid, without assuming it stays clear.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: a first measurement concept that handles this change rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear

customer_premises.claim: Laboratory results are an adequate reference for the spectroscopic measurement.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: with laboratory results used as the reference

unknowns: Protein concentration range and the species/fraction that must be tracked
Whey matrix composition and interfering components (fats, solids, other dissolved species)
Degree, cause and dynamics of the turbidity change
Temperature and pressure at the measurement point
Exact installation point and distance from the concentration stage
Cleaning regime (e.g. CIP) and fouling behaviour
Required accuracy, precision and response time
Reference laboratory method, sampling procedure, uncertainty and turnaround time
Flow rate, line size and piping geometry
